title: Marching in parades
summary: He led a brass band with violin in carnival parades, played advertising wagons, and enjoyed band contests; Big Eye Louis called him a jazz fiddler.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Did you ever march in any parades in New Orleans?
Yes, I played with them. I've led the brass band with violin.
What was violin?

Out on the street? Out on the street, I had my, they hired my band. That's all there's an issue with them. Well, I had to hire three more to make ten pieces, you know. And you took your violin out. I did some walking that carnival. For the Jefferson City budget. You know where they are up there on Annunciation Street.
I follow them almost every year. I still go there. Is it Annunciation they're on? Yeah, I'm pretty sure. About 5100 blocks. 5100 blocks.
Dufaucet, around Dufaucet Annunciation. Long in there.
The Lions Club is in there too.
Lions Club.
Near Lions, right in there.
Now, you know, that's a walk from there way below Canal Street. They'd pass on Canal Street and everything. And then I'd come back.
Would you bow in?
Could you play that walking all around? Just walk a piece and then this
caramol.
The multi-parades we used to play in the wagon trucks.
Oh, yeah.
Of course, a lot of them we played in horse and wagons too. Advertising for different dances. all around through town sign on each side of the truck. Did a plenty of that.
Do you ever get caught in one of those contests they talk about?
Run into another band where they'd buck at the corner? Often.
We used to do that often. But I had, I had a good, good jazz crew. I didn't care about that. I used to like it.
Hold you on on it.

I was a jazz fiddler. Sometimes fellas used to think of the clarinet. That's what Big Al Louie used to say when he used to hire me. Come, little lady, say, I thought there was a clarinet. You know, wait, Bill, you'd have that fiddle going. You know Big Al Louie, don't you?
